Collectopus

Collectopus Privacy Policy

Effective date: 1 October 2026
Last updated: 5 October 2026
Controller: Kirillov & Co (Maksim Kirillov, individual developer, Ukraine), contact: collectoctopus@gmail.com

1. What Collectopus does

Collectopus lets you photograph real-world objects and turn them into collectible cards.

2. Data we collect

  • Photos you take in the app. Before anything leaves your phone, the app looks for human faces on your device. If a person is the main subject of the photo, nothing is uploaded. Faces that the app detects elsewhere in the photo are pixelated and blurred on your device before upload. A reduced copy of the photo (max 512 px, location metadata removed) is sent to our server and, through OpenRouter, to Google's Gemini model on Google Cloud Vertex AI only to recognize the object; we do not store it. We do not store the original photo either. We store only the card picture: the cut-out of the object or, if it can't be cut out, a square crop of the photo with detected faces blurred.
  • Account data: an anonymous account ID; your nickname and avatar card (one of your own cards). If you choose to sign in with Google, our sign-in service (Supabase Auth) keeps the details Google provides for that account — your name, email address, Google account ID and a link to your Google profile picture — only to sign you in. We do not copy them into the game, and other players never see them: in the game you appear only with your own nickname and avatar card.
  • Approximate location (optional): if you allow it, the app asks only for approximate location, and only when you open City sets or turn it on in Settings. Turning it off in Settings erases your city from our server. Your phone sends a rough position (rounded to about 1 km) to our server, which looks up the city and country in its own offline list of cities. We store only the city and country; the coordinates are not stored, not logged and not shared with any third party.
  • Gameplay data: your cards, collections, points, streaks, friends, event progress.
  • Purchases: subscription and purchase status via Google Play and RevenueCat. We do not receive your payment card details.
  • Diagnostics and analytics: crash reports (Firebase Crashlytics) are always sent, because we need them to keep the app working. Anonymous usage events (PostHog) are optional: in the EU/UK (and when your phone looks European) the app asks first and sends nothing until you agree; everyone can turn them off in Profile → Settings → Usage statistics.
  • On-device recognition (Google ML Kit): face detection and cutting out the object run on your phone. ML Kit sends Google anonymous diagnostics about how these tools work — device and app information, performance, error codes and a per-installation identifier — never your photos.
  • Push token if you allow notifications. Turning notifications off in Settings removes it from our server.
  • Waitlist (website): if you join the waitlist on https://playcollectopus.github.io/, we store your email address, your browser's language, which link brought you to the site (for example a TikTok, Instagram or YouTube link) and the sign-up date. We use your email only to tell you when Collectopus launches and to invite you to test it, never for anything else, and we do not share it with anyone. To stop bots, our server keeps a scrambled (hashed) form of your IP address for one hour; the IP address itself is not stored.

3. How we use data

To provide the game, recognize photos, run leaderboards and events, process subscriptions, send notifications you enabled, fix bugs and improve the app. We do not sell personal data and do not use your photos to train AI models. The reduced photo goes through OpenRouter, which does not store the request, to Google Gemini on Vertex AI with Zero Data Retention: Google does not store it after answering and does not use it to train or improve its models.

4. Processors

Supabase (hosting, database, storage — servers in Frankfurt, EU), OpenRouter (forwards the reduced photo to Google for recognition, United States; no storage of requests), Google (Gemini on Vertex AI, Firebase, ML Kit diagnostics, Google Play), PostHog (analytics, EU region), RevenueCat (subscriptions), GitHub (hosting of our website and invite links). They process data on our behalf under their terms. Some of them may process data outside your country, including in the United States; where required, such transfers rely on the providers' standard contractual clauses or equivalent safeguards.

5. Who can see your data

Friends you add can see your nickname, avatar, cards and points. You can block a player or report a nickname; a reported nickname is hidden until we review it, and reports are kept only until they are reviewed. City leaderboards (if enabled) show your nickname and weekly points to other players in your city. Nobody sees your location.

6. Retention

We keep your data while your account exists. Deleting your account removes your profile, cards, images and friendships within 30 days (removal from backups may take up to 30 more days).
Waitlist email addresses are kept until Collectopus launches on Google Play plus 6 months, then deleted. To be removed from the waitlist earlier, email collectoctopus@gmail.com from that address and we will delete it.

7. Your rights

You can access, correct or delete your data: in the app (Settings → Delete account) or at https://playcollectopus.github.io/delete-account/ or by email to collectoctopus@gmail.com. EU/UK users have rights under GDPR, including objection and complaint to a supervisory authority.

8. Children

Collectopus is intended for users aged 13 and older. We do not knowingly collect data from children under 13. If you believe a child under 13 has used the app, contact us and we will delete the account.

9. Changes

We will notify you in the app about material changes.

10. Contact
